traceability.notes:
The story docs/stories/002.0-DEV-ESLINT-CONFIG.story.md specifies ESLint configuration presets, flat config alignment, customization, validation, and documentation.
Mapping to acceptance criteria and requirements: - Core Functionality / REQ-CONFIG-PRESETS: The plugin exposes `configs.recommended` and `configs.strict` in src/index.ts as ESLint flat-config presets built from a shared severity map. Tests in tests/plugin-default-export-and-configs.test.ts verify that the presets exist, that the default export exposes `configs`, and that both presets contain the expected rule keys and severities, with `strict` mirroring `recommended`. - Quality Standards / REQ-FLAT-CONFIG: The presets are implemented as ESLint v9 flat config arrays (`recommended: [configObject]`, `strict: [configObject]`). README.md and user-docs/eslint-9-setup-guide.md consistently demonstrate ESLint v9 flat config patterns and explicitly show `eslint.config.js` usage including `traceability.configs.recommended` and `traceability.configs.strict`. - Integration / REQ-PROJECT-INTEGRATION: The ESLint 9 Setup Guide provides concrete flat-config examples for JavaScript projects, TypeScript projects, mixed JS/TS, Node config files, test files, and monorepo/workspace setups, each showing how to integrate the plugin alongside other configs like `@eslint/js`. This supports seamless integration with various existing ESLint setups and project structures. - User Experience & Documentation: README.md links to the ESLint 9 Setup Guide and includes quick-start flat config examples using the plugin presets. user-docs/eslint-9-setup-guide.md and docs/config-presets.md supply comprehensive configuration examples, common patterns, and a dedicated troubleshooting section for ESLint flat configuration, satisfying the documentation and UX-related acceptance criteria. - Error Handling & Validation / REQ-CUSTOMIZABLE-PATHS / REQ-RULE-OPTIONS / REQ-CONFIG-VALIDATION: The rules that are configurable under this story expose JSON Schema via `meta.schema` for their options. `valid-story-reference` supports `storyDirectories`, `allowAbsolutePaths`, and `requireStoryExtension`, with `additionalProperties: false`, and uses those options at runtime to control path handling and validation. `require-story-annotation` similarly exposes `scope` and `exportPriority` with `additionalProperties: false`. Tests in tests/config/eslint-config-validation.test.ts and tests/config/require-story-annotation-config.test.ts (annotated with this story) assert that the schemas define the expected properties and explicitly verify that unknown options are disallowed, showing graceful and predictable handling of invalid configuration. This matches REQ-RULE-OPTIONS, REQ-CUSTOMIZABLE-PATHS, and REQ-CONFIG-VALIDATION.
Taken together, the implemented presets, schema-validated rule options, configurable story paths, flat-config-centric documentation, and story-tagged tests demonstrate that all acceptance criteria and listed requirements for 002.0-DEV-ESLINT-CONFIG have been implemented and are verified by automated tests. Therefore, the assessment status is PASSED.
